name: Prezi
tagline: Presentation, video, and design tools with a zooming visual canvas

pricing.basis: paid plan; billing basis requires review
pricing.native: Public paid plan exists; amount not safely recovered
pricing.notes: The official pricing URL is recorded, but a stable current amount was not safely recoverable in this pass. Do not publish a number until rechecked.

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.limits: Up to 5 editable presentations; 500 AI credits; up to 10 talking points per AI presentation.
tiers.notes: Basic content lacks paid privacy controls.

tiers.name: Standard
tiers.limits: 500 AI credits; up to 10 talking points; privacy controls.
tiers.notes: Displayed as $7/month billed annually; a month-to-month price was not exposed.

tiers.name: Plus
tiers.limits: Unlimited AI presentation generation; desktop/offline app; PDF export and personal branding.
tiers.notes: Displayed as $19/month billed annually; a month-to-month price was not exposed.

tiers.name: Premium
tiers.limits: Unlimited AI presentation generation; Plus features; analytics and phone support.
tiers.notes: Displayed as $29/month billed annually; a month-to-month price was not exposed.

tiers.name: Edu Plus
tiers.limits: Unlimited AI presentation generation; certified education email required.
tiers.notes: Sold at an education discount, but the accessible public page did not expose the current price.

tiers.name: Edu Pro
tiers.limits: Edu Plus plus analytics, exclusive support and advanced import integrations.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: Premium features plus centralized billing; teams with 10+ licences receive custom templates and branded designs.

tiers.name: Edu Teams
tiers.limits: Edu Plus features plus analytics and enhanced collaboration.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 5 editable presentations; 500 AI credits; up to 10 talking points; content loses paid privacy controls
pricing.billingTerms: annual billing for published Standard, Plus and Premium rates; 14-day trial; education and team pricing is quote/check-out based
pricing.hiddenCosts: paid plans auto-renew; after expiry content remains stored but cannot be edited or newly created until renewal or downgrade; team customization starts at 10 licences

verdictSummary: The visible zooming presentations loop is buildable, but a credible replacement needs more than the first screen. Prezi earns its keep through interaction polish, collaboration, so expect a weekend or multi-day build and a narrower personal scope.
coreLoopDIY: Build a browser-based zooming presentations editor with drag, resize, connect, keyboard shortcuts, autosave, and SVG or PNG export.
replacementScope: narrow personal or very small-team substitute
whatYouLose: production codecs, rendering speed, and media templates
whyPeopleStillPay: Prezi: The shapes are easy; customers pay for low-friction editing, reliable exports, collaboration, and a canvas that never fights them.
ongoingBurden: Own geometry, selection behavior, undo, clipboard interoperability, export fidelity, accessibility, and browser performance.

priorArt.name: Excalidraw
priorArt.desc: Open-source diagram canvas with an approachable interaction model.

alternatives.name: Sozi
alternatives.desc: A real zooming presentation editor built around SVG canvases and camera paths; less collaborative, less glossy, and blessedly free of a monthly bill.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Excalidraw
rejectedAlternatives.desc: It provides an infinite canvas and presentation-like frames, but not Prezi's sequenced zoom paths and polished playback model.

notes: Useful boundary case: the first 60 percent of Prezi is approachable, but operating the last 40 percent is the real subscription.
prompt:
Build a deliberately narrow personal substitute for Prezi, not a full clone.
Use exactly this stack: React + TypeScript + Vite + IndexedDB.
Primary job: Build a browser-based zooming presentations editor with drag, resize, connect, keyboard shortcuts, autosave, and SVG or PNG export.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: presentation and enterprise controls; production codecs, rendering speed, and media templates; multiplayer cursors and comments.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
